# Launch windows report

Computed by `scripts/generators/gen_launch_windows.py` (Global Commons spec § 5.3, § 5.2a) for 1900.01 to 2136.01. A window is the Hohmann optimum's calendar month and the months either side. Premiums are `exp(extra delta-v / 3.7 km/s) - 1` against the cycle's best window month, the extra delta-v averaged over 16 cycles spread across the span; the spread is the range of the individual cycles' premiums. Delta-v: departure from a 200 km parking orbit, capture into an orbit of eccentricity 0.9 at a tenth of a radius up at a planet, rendezvous at a small body.

## The off-window rule on Mars

A full bar launches outside a window when goal × premium ÷ pace ≤ k × m (Standard k = 1, Ambitious 2; m = months to the next free window), in a 26-month cycle, goal 400:

| Pace | Standard launches | Ambitious launches |
|---|---|---|
| 5 a month | in the window only (3 in 26) | 2 months after (4 in 26) |
| 10 a month | 2 months after (4 in 26) | 2 months after (4 in 26) |
| 20 a month | 2 months after (4 in 26) | 2–3 months after (5 in 26) |
| 40 a month | 2–3 months after (5 in 26) | 2–10 months after (12 in 26) |

## Transit times

The months a colony fleet takes (solar colonization slices 2-3 design § 2), rounded, at least 1. Chemical is the body's median Hohmann time, whatever the month. Fusion (Fusion Power): the shortest Lambert transfer within 30 km/s, from 0.05 to 2.6 times the Hohmann time. Fusion torch (Muon-Catalyzed Fusion Reactors): a brachistochrone at 0.01 g, its delta-v capped at 400 km/s. Antimatter (Antimatter Production and an Antimatter Containment Facility): a brachistochrone at 0.03 g, its delta-v capped at 2,000 km/s. By months from the optimum, a departure on day 15 averaged over the premium's cycles; a better drive is never slower than the one before it.

| Body | Chemical | Fusion, in a window | Fusion torch, in a window | Antimatter, in a window |
